questions.question: Leaking shock absorbers:

options.text: Will stop the turn signals from working.
Are safe if you only drive on highways.

questions.explanation: The suspension system holds a vehicle's axles in place. Damaged suspension parts, like leaking shock absorbers, are dangerous and can fail.

questions.question: If the emergency air line loses pressure, it will:
questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. If air pressure is lost, the emergency trailer brakes will activate.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Is needed to warm up vehicle parts.

questions.explanation: Always speed up slowly and smoothly. Rough acceleration can cause damage to your vehicle.

questions.question: Steering wheel play should not be more than:
questions.explanation: A steering wheel should have no more than 10 degrees of play, which is about two inches of movement on a 20-inch wheel. More play than this makes steering difficult.

questions.question: The best way to avoid glare from oncoming headlights at night is to:

options.text: Close your eyes as vehicles approach.
Look to the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: To avoid being blinded by oncoming lights, glance to the right side of the road until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:

options.text: Keep your vehicle in front of them.

questions.explanation: Do not be provoked by an aggressive driver's actions or gestures. Do not make eye contact. Get out of their way if you can do so safely.

questions.question: Placards must be placed:

options.text: Within three inches of other markings.
So words and numbers read from left to right.

questions.correctAnswerText: So words and numbers read from left to right.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be at least three inches away from other markings and positioned so words and numbers are level and read from left to right.

questions.question: How much space should there be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?

options.text: A maximum of two inches of space.

questions.explanation: When inspecting couplings before a trip, there should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: When doing a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Always follow the same steps in the same order.
Complete it as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always follow the same steps in the same order.
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This helps you remember all the important steps and prevents you from missing anything.

questions.question: If you notice hazardous materials leaking while driving, you should:

options.text: Park the vehicle as soon as possible.
Leave the area to find help.
Drive around looking for someone to repair the leak.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park the vehicle as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: If a cargo leak develops, stop driving immediately. The farther you drive, the larger the contaminated area becomes. Park the vehicle, secure the area, and send someone else to get help.

questions.question: How can you best tell if your trailer is skidding?

options.text: By looking at other drivers' faces.
By watching the trailer in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: By watching the trailer in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Watch your trailer in your mirrors. This is the easiest way to spot a skid early.

questions.question: What happens if an engine runs without oil?

options.text: The vehicle will get better gas mileage.
The engine can be destroyed quickly.
The Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) won't work properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine can be destroyed quickly.
questions.explanation: An engine needs oil to work. Without it, the engine can be destroyed very fast.

questions.question: What causes the most deaths and injuries in work zones?
questions.explanation: Drivers going too fast cause most deaths and injuries in work zones. Slow down when driving through a work zone.

questions.question: How should you drive a heavy vehicle to avoid blocking traffic?

options.text: Pass other vehicles while driving uphill.
Ride the brakes while driving downhill.

questions.explanation: If your heavy vehicle cannot match traffic speed, stay in the right lane when possible.

questions.question: What should windshield wiper blades be when you check them?
questions.explanation: Check that wiper blades are secure and not damaged. Clean them if they are dirty.

questions.question: What should you do when traveling long distances?
questions.explanation: Take a break every 100 miles or every 2 hours to avoid fatigue. Driving when you are normally asleep is dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do if you need to stop on the road to unload cargo?

options.text: Stop suddenly, since you are already on the road.
Tap your brakes to warn other drivers.
Wave your arm out the window to get drivers' attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brakes to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Tap your brakes and flash your brake lights to warn other drivers when you plan to slow or stop unexpectedly.

questions.question: What should you do after a trip?
questions.explanation: You may be required to inspect the vehicle and file a report after each trip.

questions.question: What is the best way to check your lights during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Park near a mirror to see a reflection.
Turn on the lights, then get out and look at them.
Look at the instrument panel for warning lights.
Drive in traffic and wait for other drivers to tell you if lights are out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the lights, then get out and look at them.
questions.explanation: Turn on your lights, then exit the vehicle to check them during a pre-trip inspection.

questions.question: What affects your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Your speed affects stopping distance. The vehicle's weight and road surface also affect stopping distance.

questions.question: When you start a truck with a trailer, how do you know if the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working?

options.text: The yellow light on the back of the trailer stays on.
The red light on the trailer flashes three times and then stays on.
All the rear lights on the trailer flash and then turn off.
The blue light near the driver's door turns on.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the back of the trailer stays on.
questions.explanation: Trailers with ABS have a yellow warning light on the left rear. If this light stays on after the engine starts, the ABS is not working properly.

questions.question: When it is hard for others to see your vehicle, such as at dawn or dusk, you can help other drivers by:

options.text: Waving your arm out the window.

questions.explanation: When it is hard to see, turn on your headlights. If you cannot see other vehicles, they cannot see you either.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor that drives faster than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a trailer. These are hard to control, so drivers must be careful.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It lets a vehicle's wheels lock up.
It stops a vehicle's wheels from locking up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops a vehicle's wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents wheel lockup when braking hard. If ABS senses wheels are about to lock, it reduces brake pressure to keep the wheels moving.

questions.question: A thin layer of ice that forms on road surfaces is called:
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road through it, so it may just look wet. Be careful when temperatures drop below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: Eating while driving:

options.text: Is a good idea on long trips.
Takes your attention away from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Eating while driving is dangerous. It distracts you and requires you to take one hand off the steering wheel.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a problem with an exhaust system?

options.text: Exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts.
Exhaust system parts that are not leaking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts that are not leaking.
questions.explanation: When checking the exhaust system, make sure all parts are secure and not loose, broken, or missing. Parts must be properly mounted and not touching moving parts of the vehicle.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice that forms on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road through it, so it may just look wet. Be careful when temperatures drop below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: Rims with welding repairs:

options.text: Are safe to use on the rear of the vehicle.
Are safe to use if you carry a light load.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims with welding repairs are never safe to use.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill, what should be your main way to control your speed?
questions.explanation: On a steep downhill grade, use the engine's braking power to control your speed. Downshift and slow down before you start going downhill.
